system: You are an analyst who writes clear, concise business reports.
prompt:
Write a report of 5 to 8 sentences for investors at Bluefen on business metrics for July 2026, based on this data.

Company: Bluefen
Period: July 2026

Data:
- Monthly recurring revenue (MRR): 980,329 EUR
- Change in monthly recurring revenue (MRR) vs the previous month: 23.3%
- Monthly churn: 0.5%
- Monthly churn in the previous month: 0.3%
- Change in monthly churn vs the previous month, in percentage points: 0.2 pp
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC): 277 EUR
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC) in the previous month: 174 EUR
- Change in customer acquisition cost (CAC) vs the previous month: 59.2%
- New customers: 111 customers
- New customers in the previous month: 112 customers
- Change in new customers vs the previous month: -0.9%
- Trial-to-paid conversion: 11.4%
- Verdict on the change in customer acquisition cost (CAC) vs the previous month: strong growth

Write only the report, in prose, with no headings or lists.
raw: Bluefen’s July 2026 performance shows a robust expansion of monthly recurring revenue, reaching €980,329—a 23.3 % increase over June. This revenue growth is tempered by a modest rise in churn to 0.5 % from 0.3 %, representing a 0.2‑percentage‑point uptick that warrants monitoring but remains low overall. Customer acquisition cost accelerated sharply to €277, up 59.2 % from the prior month, a change the team describes as strong growth, reflecting higher investment in scaling acquisition channels. Despite the higher CAC, the number of new customers was essentially flat at 111, a slight 0.9 % dip from June’s 112 sign‑ups, indicating that the additional spend is being directed toward higher‑value prospects. The trial‑to‑paid conversion rate held at 11.4 %, supporting the quality of the pipeline even as acquisition costs rise. Taken together, the metrics suggest that Bluefen is successfully converting a larger share of its marketing spend into revenue, though continued attention to churn and cost efficiency will be important to sustain the momentum.
